findings.evidence: This skill is a **Process** ... executed with **Tool-level rigor** at each step
findings.fix: Remove the self-classification and retain the practical reason to use the factory subcommands.

findings.evidence: Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup or when ai-kit-spec-review warns no config exists.
findings.fix: Set up and check ai-kit's cross-AI review and execute lanes: discover CLIs and models, choose a fallback order, check reviewer availability and provider warnings, and write or migrate config.toml and review-spec.toml. Use when configuring or refreshing reviewers or executors, checking availability without saving, investigating stale providers, or migrating an old roster, even if the user does not call it cross-AI setup. Supports --check-only, --local and --global. Not for running a review or changing unrelated ai-kit settings.

findings.evidence: The negative queries include "Write a unit test for the parser in the markdown-to-pdf skill" and "Explain how git rebase differs from git merge in simple terms," but no nearby cross-AI execution or unrelated config tasks.
findings.fix: Replace several unrelated negatives with realistic near-misses such as running an existing cross-AI review, editing unrelated config.toml tables, and configuring an opencode provider independently of ai-kit.

findings.evidence: "Asks for explicit confirmation before writing the global config.toml in the ai-kit config directory" is unconditional, while SKILL.md requires replacement consent only when a roster already exists.
findings.fix: Specify an existing global roster in the eval input and assert replacement consent for that case; add a separate empty-target case matching the documented target-selection behavior.

findings.evidence: The write-risk check reads profiles for the raw target's listed entries, but "probe-quota cannot probe a subset" and "always runs the full cfg_resolve merge"; a merged entry from the other config layer can therefore be probed without its write risk being checked.
findings.fix: Determine the complete effective set that probe-quota will invoke without making live calls, check the risk of every entry in that set, and obtain consent before the probe if any has unconfirmed write permissions.

findings.evidence: CATALOG_JSON is assigned in one shell block and used in later shell blocks, although SKILL.md says "Every Bash call starts a fresh shell"; FILTERED_RUNTIMES_JSON has the same problem.
findings.fix: Capture both generated absolute paths as literal values and substitute them into later calls, as Step 0 requires for its four paths, or explicitly combine the dependent commands in one shell call.

findings.evidence: The session-default instructions say an absent purpose "matches both review and execute," whereas references/config-file.md says "review, or no purpose at all, goes to [[lanes.review]]."
findings.fix: Verify the consumer's legacy-default behavior and make the main instructions and config reference state the same actual behavior.
